question: Indicate which characteristic of the whiplash direction of the nystagmus is characteristic of an acute peripheral non-positional vestibular syndrome:

options.opa: With visual fixation and in the primary position of the gaze changes or alternates the direction spontaneously and periodically.
options.opb: With visual fixation, it changes direction when looking to one side or the other.
options.opc: With visual fixation and in the primary position of the gaze it is vertical downwards pure, without horizontal component.
options.opd: Both with visual fixation and when canceling it is unidirectional.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Acute peripheral non-positional vestibular syndrome -> nystagmus -> Nystagmus with visual fixation and in the primary position of the gaze changes or alternates direction spontaneously and periodically -> 80%
CHAIN: Acute peripheral non-positional vestibular syndrome -> nystagmus -> Nystagmus with visual fixation, it changes direction when looking to one side or the other -> 70%

CHAIN: Acute peripheral non-positional vestibular syndrome -> nystagmus -> Nystagmus with visual fixation and in the primary position of the gaze is vertical downwards pure, without a horizontal component -> 60%
CHAIN: Acute peripheral non-positional vestibular syndrome -> nystagmus -> Nystagmus both with visual fixation and when canceling it is unidirectional -> 75%
analysis: In an acute peripheral non-positional vestibular syndrome, nystagmus typically changes direction when visual fixation is removed, indicating a unidirectional nystagmus.
